rootCause: The production driver scheduled SPEC_READINESS after execution COMPLETE, accepted readiness only when execution state was COMPLETE, and benchmark finalization required exactly that terminal readiness placement. This inverted the lifecycle readiness checkpoint and skipped it between initialization and planning.
semanticOrMechanical: mechanical driver orchestration against lifecycle operation semantics

correction: Schedule one official SPEC_READINESS immediately after passing SPEC_INIT; accept it only with active ready lifecycle state and execution EMPTY; then use the official execution handoff to PLAN. After execution reaches COMPLETE, go directly to SPEC_CLOSE. Finalization now requires exactly one PASS/GLOBAL_READY immediately after INIT, PLAN immediately after readiness, COMPLETE as the last execution event, and one successful CLOSE immediately after COMPLETE. CLOSE's existing final-Q readiness and strict attestation requirements remain unchanged.
